subject: Civil Engineering
title: Tunnel Emergency Egress
description: A micro-lesson that makes Tunnel Emergency Egress usable.

hook.text: In a tunnel emergency, there's no shoulder to pull over and no exit ramp. Egress is designed in.

buildup.text: Emergency recesses — small alcoves with phones and extinguishers — line tunnel walls.

discovery.text: Cross-passages to parallel tunnels or escape galleries provide protected evacuation routes.

twist.text: Pressurized escape galleries keep smoke out — overpressure blows clean air toward evacuees.

climax.text: The Gotthard Base Tunnel has emergency stations every 10 miles with vehicle access for rescue.

punchline.text: The way out is planned before the tunnel is built. Escape is an engineering problem.

quiz.question: How do pressurized escape galleries protect evacuees during a fire?
options: They cool the air to prevent burns during evacuation
Overpressure blows clean air outward, keeping smoke from entering the escape route
They flood with water to extinguish any fire that enters
